Resurrect

/rez-uh-REKT/ — rhymes with fleck, stress on third syllable · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To resurrect something is to bring it back after it seemed to be finished, forgotten, or dead.

The studio resurrected the old cartoon with a modern movie.

Worked Example

Decades after the radio drama had vanished from airwaves, a streaming service resurrected it, and millions of new listeners discovered the original episodes.

Resurrect conveys the sense of something being truly gone, finished, or dead and then brought back to existence. Revive suggests something merely sleeping or paused, while resurrect implies finality and a miraculous return.

How Resurrect Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

Antonyms

bury

extinguish

extinguish: to put an end to something completely

How Strong Is It? — recall → revive → resurrect → immortalize

recall vs. resurrect

recall vs. resurrect: Recall is much weaker than resurrect: to recall something is only to remember it, while to resurrect it is to actually bring it back to life.

revive vs. resurrect

revive vs. resurrect: Revive is weaker than resurrect — reviving refreshes something that was fading, but resurrecting brings back something that seemed completely finished or dead.

immortalize vs. resurrect

immortalize vs. resurrect: Immortalize is stronger than resurrect: resurrecting something gives it a second life, but immortalizing it makes it live on forever, beyond any death at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again, back (Latin)

Root — surrect

Root — surrect: to rise (past stem of surgere) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Resurrect combines re- ('again') with the Latin root surrect-, from surgere ('to rise'): to resurrect something is to make it rise again after it seemed dead, finished, or forgotten.

Use the root in a new word: surge

Use the root in a new word: surge: When a crowd surges forward, it rises and rushes ahead — the same Latin root surgere, 'to rise,' that lets a resurrected tradition rise again from its end.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Resurrect is for bringing back something that seemed completely gone, finished, or dead—whether literally or figuratively (a cancelled show, a forgotten tradition, a lost custom). For something merely paused or sleeping, revive is gentler and more precise.
